title: Containment and Rollforward: Fanout Misrouting Caused Microburst Throughput Cliff
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-01 we observed repeated P95/P99 throughput cliffs during a scheduled capacity expansion window. A microburst pattern caused the runtime to route a subset of requests to a rarely-used kernel variant with a quantized-attention fallback. That fallback had poor microbatch packing behavior and triggered a KV-cache invalidation cascade across the new workers, amplifying latency and reducing overall throughput by ~42% for affected shards for 18 minutes.

Impact: Customer-facing latency spikes and throttled throughput on hosted inference routes for 3 enterprise customers and multiple internal smoke tests. No data loss, but increased cost due to emergency scale and degraded SLA adherence.

What happened (concise): Autoscaler added new workers with mixed kernel visibility. The path-selection probe on warmup misclassified the new workers as "probe-eligible" and routed a non-trivial fanout of short-sequence requests to a quantized-attn kernel variant that under-packed microbatches (created many tiny microbatches). The tiny microbatches caused increased per-token overhead and frequent KV cache churn. Runtime heuristics then preferred the fallback path, causing positive feedback and a throughput cliff until the autoscaler and admission controls stabilized.
acceptance_criteria: Deployment has a safe rollforward that eliminates the misrouting on warm worker join
Autoscaler warmup no longer exposes probe-eligible state before KV cache warm assertions pass
New canary demonstrates stable P95/P99 under simulated microburst traffic for 48 hours
Follow-up telemetry added to detect similar fanout/cliff patterns within 5 minutes
updates: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Incident detected by Canary heartbeat alerts (p95 throughput drop). Notified oncall and paged runtime team.
2026-03-01 09:20 - Initial triage: pattern looks like worker-join correlated with latency spike. Scoped to specific model family and short context lengths.
2026-03-01 10:05 - Rolled containment: disabled speculative probing on new workers and limited probe fanout to 1%. That reduced the worst-of-cliff immediately.
2026-03-01 11:30 - Emergency rollforward: rolled back recent kernel-ranking tweak that increased probe aggressiveness. This restored normal p95 within 12 minutes.

2026-03-02 14:00 - Post-incident reproduction attempts succeeded in synthetic harness; confirmed microbatch underpacking behavior when microbatcher sees <3 tokens per request and quantized fallback enabled.
2026-03-05 16:40 - Patch PR opened to gate probe eligibility on KV-cache-warm and microbatch-packing-stability signals (PR #1298).
2026-03-09 09:00 - Internal review with PM and SRE: agreed to a two-phase rollout (canary -> gradual) and to add a runtime circuit to limit serial fanout when microbatch packing efficiency < 0.6.
2026-03-11 08:30 - This ticket moved to In Review. Patch and telemetry merged to canary cluster; monitoring dashboards updated.
decisions: Immediate rollback of probe-aggressiveness kernel ranking change (decision: rollback to last stable commit SHA abc123).
Gate speculative probing on new workers until KV-cache-warm AND microbatch-packing-stable signals both true.
Implement a short-term circuit breaker that limits probe fanout to 1% on worker joins and to 0.5% when microbatch packing efficiency < 0.6.
Adopt rollforward as primary remediation instead of long rollback to permit a faster recovery path for small escalations.
